q: Which crate implements the MCP protocol for goose (client and built-in servers)?
explanation: mcp_utils.rs is goose's small helper layer over rmcp types.

q: What does `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION = ProtocolVersion::V_2025_11_25` do for the codebase?
options: Pins the protocol revision for every MCP handshake, so a spec bump is a one-line change
It is a UI label only
explanation: Providers have their own envelopes; this constant is MCP-specific.
TLS is transport config (goose/src/config/tls.rs).
The constant flows into client initialization, not just labels.

q: Why does goose maintain its own `McpClient` wrapper instead of using rmcp's client directly?
options: To layer goose concerns — capabilities tracking, structured errors, cancellation, tool-call enrichment — behind one McpClientTrait seam
Because rmcp has no client at all
Because goose is written in Python
explanation: rmcp ships a full client; goose wraps it (see impl ClientHandler for GooseClient).
rmcp is an open-source dependency; licensing isn't the reason.
Goose is Rust; the whole repo is a cargo workspace.

q: What is a dangling `$ref` in a tool's input schema, and why does `inline_refs` exist?
options: A reference to a definition never included in the schema; some provider models can't resolve refs, so goose inlines definitions before sending
A provider auth token that expired
explanation: Lifetimes are Rust concepts; JSON Schema never sees them.
Token expiry is auth, not schema.
readOnly is an annotation; a dangling $ref is a broken pointer.

options: A plain `enum` list of the const values — the dialect that older tools emit, normalized
explanation: Tuples aren't part of this repair output.
The union isn't dropped — it's converted to enum form.
Percent-encoding repair applies to $defs keys, not values.

options: In-process rmcp ServerHandlers served over stdio, registered in goose-mcp's BUILTIN_EXTENSIONS

q: Fix this integration failure: a third-party stdio server percent-encodes its `$defs` keys (`my%20def`), and tool schemas are garbled downstream. Which module already handles this?
options: tool_schema_normalize.rs — percent_decode decodes the keys before processing (no server-side fix required)
The server must be rewritten (goose has no decode step)
explanation: percent_decode exists precisely to avoid forcing server rewrites.
subprocess.rs handles spawning, not schema text.
rename_all is for Rust struct serde, not server schema keys.
